newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: THREDBO LODGES FACE DEMOLITION IN WAKE OF DISASTER INQUIRY
Several lodges at the Thredbo resort may have to be demolished pending the outcome of a coronial inquiry.
Coronial investigators have begun compiling a database on the stability of buildings and land surrounding the disaster site.
More machinery has been brought on to the landslide site to speed up clearing earth and debris.
Meanwhile, an ecumenical prayer and reflection gathering will be held today for the friends and families of those involved in the tragedy.
The Governor-General, political leaders and church dignatories will attend the gathering at the Thredbo Village Chapel.
Church leaders have stressed it will be a prayer and reflection gathering and not a memorial service.
FREEMAN ONLY AUSSIE ATHLETE TO REACH FINALS
Cathy Freeman is the only Australian athlete to progress to a final in the world track and field championships in Athens.

Freeman finished third in her 400-metres semi-final with a time of 50.11. She was beaten in a close finish by American Jearl Miles-Clark and Olympic bronze medallist Falilat Ogunkoya. Sprinter Melinda Gainsford-Taylor has failed to qualify for the 100-metres final, despite posting a time of 10.35 and coming sixth in the faster semi-final.
Margaret Crowley also missed out on a semi-final place when she came ninth in her heat of the 1500-metres event.
But Freeman, who said she was "a bit pooped" after her race, said she wanted to prove something ahead of tomorrow's final.
"It's always a bit more passionate in a semi; everybody's scrambling for a place in the final," she said.
CONCERN AS HIV PATIENTS AVOID TREATMENT
AIDS educators believe less than half the number of people living with HIV in Australia are seeking treatments.
Bad experience with drugs like AZT, little access to information and a view that the virus can remain dormant in the body are reasons given for the poor compliance rate.
A new booklet, HIV Tests and Treatments, launched in Melbourne last night, will be distributed nationally to encourage more gay men and injecting drug users to seek a range of new treatments.
CARR PROMISES MORE NEW JOBS FOR NEWCASTLE
New South Wales Premier Bob Carr will visit Newcastle this morning with a promise to help create 2,500 jobs by 2000.
The Hunter Valley region has been hit by BHP's decison to close its steel-making facility in 1999, costing more than 2,000 jobs.
But 120 jobs will be created following a decision by pharmaceutical company Jurox to expand its operations in Maitland.
Mr Carr said that was the first initiative under his government's $10 million Hunter Advantage Scheme.
The scheme was established in this year's State budget following the BHP decision.
DONORS RALLY TO SALVATION ARMY APPEAL CHALLENGE
The Salvation Army has raised more than $38 million in its annual Red Shield Appeal.
Major Margaret Armstrong, the officer in charge of fund-raising, said the amount was up on previous years. She said the result was particularly pleasing in Victoria.
"Victorians are always generous to the appeal," she said.
"This year, about a month ago, we were $880,000 short of goal, and many of our donors who give through the mail program responded with open hearts and just helped us to achieve the goal this year."
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
